reviews.review:
[H1]Perfect if you like easy HOGs, except maybe for the mildly grating partner[/H1]

This is a hard one to talk about because it’s very clearly made for a very specific crowd. The gameplay itself is extremely easy. Like, kid-level easy. The hidden object scenes barely hide anything and the puzzles never push back, which feels more like a guided stroll than a challenge. That would normally be totally fine…except the writing and character interactions really don’t match that child-friendly difficulty. Let me explain.

You play as a detective helping Celesta, an anthropomorphized furret, figure out why the townfolks have forgotten who they are and started acting completely unlike themselves. There are 5 cases, each splitting into multiple sublevels with a few puzzles sprinkled in, all slowly pointing toward the source of the collective amnesia. The premise is genuinely interesting and original compared to most HOGs, and it had me curious the whole way through.

Visually, it’s lovely. Everything is hand-drawn, lightly animated, and clearly made with care. No reused assets, lots of different environments, and a nice variety of items to search for. The achievements are simple and follow completion. Plus, the music and ambient sounds fit the mood well overall, even if a couple of levels go a bit too hard on loud wave sounds, which feels jarring in what’s supposed to be a relaxing experience (nothing that can't be quickly fixed in the game menu though).

Puzzle-wise, there are some fun ideas here. They’re simple, but engaging enough, and I honestly would have enjoyed them a lot more if there was just a bit more resistance. The bigger issue is that while the game feels designed for kids mechanically, there’s no hint system at all, neither for puzzles, nor hidden object scenes, which makes that audience choice a bit confusing.

And then there’s Celesta. She’s the real dealbreaker for me. She’s the one asking for your help to heal the amnesia victims, but she constantly rolls her eyes, gets angry quickly, downplays the townfolks, and shows very little empathy. That attitude never lets up, and it annoyed me pretty fast. It’s a shame, because without her personality, this could have been a very cozy, low-effort HOG for kids or adults looking for something cute and undemanding. Instead, she bugged me for the entire 2 hour run, and that frustration stuck longer than any puzzle did.

So yeah, this isn’t bad, just extremely niche. If you enjoy [i]very[/i] easy hidden object games, like a good premise, and can tolerate an unnerving main companion, this might still work for you. Just know exactly what you’re signing up for before jumping in.
